proposed.choice: Separate candidate construction and public receipt preparation from the SQLite persistence adapter.
proposed.rationale: SR-043 and SR-044 distinguish nonwriting preview from a fresh execution, while SR-046 requires a fitting receipt before authoritative replacement.
alternatives: Reusing preview bytes as publication authority or preparing receipts only after writing would fail to preserve the selected freshness and outcome boundaries.
consequences: The store owns connection configuration, project/schema checks, short write transactions and expected-revision checks. Candidate construction supplies no independent persistence authority.
Prepare the bounded receipt and validate the complete candidate before commit; abort the whole transaction on precommit failure. A committed result survives output-delivery failure.

Coordinate optional attachment publication and cleanup under database writer exclusion as specified by the owning Records contract. Repository subject observations retain their explicit external-edit limits.

The proposed software organization separates typed candidate rules, a node:sqlite adapter, named payload handling and fenced maintenance; SQL migrations are packaged product inputs, not live project data.

IF-003 v4 dispatch uses closed query/task/maintenance requests and typed outcomes. MOD-011 alone owns SQL and connection handles; precommit receipt readiness uses the fixed shared MOD-010-owned pure codec, never arbitrary caller callbacks.
revisit_when: The execution mechanism changes, requiring these freshness, authority, and receipt guarantees to be re-established.
